awd_titl_txt: Conference: Connections between Commutative and Non-commutative Harmonic Analysis
awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports U.S.-based participants in attending the workshop "Connections between Commutative and Non-commutative Harmonic Analysis," to be held at the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences (ICMS) in Edinburgh, UK, during the week of September 1–5, 2025. The workshop aims to bring together senior and early-career researchers working in commutative and non-commutative harmonic analysis. Although these fields share deep connections, their communities rarely have the opportunity to meet at conferences of this scale. The workshop will provide a unique environment to present recent advances and exchange expertise. 

This workshop will focus on four central topics in harmonic analysis: matrix weights, Fourier multipliers on (non-abelian) groups, vector-valued harmonic analysis, and martingale-related techniques. It will begin with four plenary mini-courses on these themes, delivered by leading experts. The workshop will also feature invited long and short talks by researchers working around these core topics. In addition, there will be contributed talks and a poster session to provide more opportunities for graduate students and early-career researchers to present their work. More information can be found at https://www.icms.org.uk/CommutativeandNonCommutativeHarmonicAnalysis

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
From September 1 to 5, 2025, the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences in Edinburgh, United Kingdom, hosted the workshop “Connections between Commutative and Non-commutative Harmonic Analysis.” The workshop was partially supported by NSF award DMS-2523775, which supported U.S.-based participation. Harmonic analysis studies how functions and operators can be understood through patterns of symmetry, scale, frequency, and oscillation, using Fourier series and the Fourier transform as foundational tools. The meeting connected researchers who study these questions in classical settings with researchers who study analogous questions for matrices and operators, two communities that use related ideas but do not often meet at this scale. The scientific program centered on matrix weights, Fourier multipliers on non-abelian groups, vector-valued harmonic analysis, and martingale methods.

The five-day program combined four two-part mini-courses with nine long talks, eight short talks, and a poster-and-discussion session. The mini-courses supplied broad introductions to current research directions, while the shorter presentations created space for focused results and emerging questions. The published program lists 21 named presenters from institutions in ten countries. Talks connected classical and non-commutative methods through topics including multiplier theory, matrix-weighted estimates, operator algebras, ergodic inequalities, martingales, and analysis on groups. Participant feedback posted by ICMS described the talks as motivating and reported that the meeting generated insight into new topics for future exploration.

The project’s broader impact came from lowering barriers to international participation, connecting U.S.-based mathematicians with a wider research network, and giving researchers in the early stages of their careers opportunities to present work through contributed talks and posters. The public ICMS event page preserves the full program and links to talk abstracts and presentation slides, extending the educational value of the workshop beyond those who attended. These materials provide an accessible record of the meeting and a resource for researchers and students interested in the connections between classical and non-commutative harmonic analysis.

Public event record: https://icms.ac.uk/activities/workshop/connections-between-commutative-and-non-commutative-harmonic-analysis/
